velle-css

CSS components that work with any stack. Plain CSS with design tokens and utilities, a small dependency-free JavaScript runtime for interactive pieces, and a Go CLI that copies only what you use into your project.

velle-css is a port of css-zero by Lázaro Nixon, without its dependencies on Ruby on Rails, Hotwire and Stimulus.

Installation

With the CLI

Install the velle command with Go, then run it in your project:

go install github.com/codedbyshoe/velle-css/cmd/velle@latest

velle init                  # writes velle.json and copies the core styles
velle add button dialog     # copies components and everything they need
velle list                  # shows every component

velle init puts files in assets/css/velle, assets/js/velle and assets/images/velle. Choose other directories with --css-dir, --js-dir and --images-dir, or edit velle.json later. velle add never replaces a file you have changed unless you pass --overwrite, and it prints the <link> and <script> tags to add to your page.

From GitHub, without the CLI

Every release includes a dist/ folder. Load everything from the jsDelivr CDN, replacing v{{.Site.Version}} with the release you want:

<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/codedbyshoe/velle-css@v{{.Site.Version}}/dist/velle.css">
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/codedbyshoe/velle-css@v{{.Site.Version}}/dist/velle.js"></script>

You can also download the repository and copy files from dist/css, dist/js and dist/images. These folders hold the same individual files the CLI installs.

Adapters

Four components wrap a third-party library: chart (Chart.js), datepicker (flatpickr), inputmask (maska) and sortable (SortableJS). velle-css ships only the adapter: the controller and its theme. You install the library and choose its version.

  • Each adapter imports its library by package name, e.g. import flatpickr from "flatpickr". With a bundler, npm install the package. Without one, add it to an import map; each adapter's page shows the exact snippet.
  • Adapters are not in dist/velle.js or dist/velle.css, so the bundles stay dependency-free. Load them from dist/adapters/, where they share the bundle's runtime, or install them with velle add, which also prints the install instructions.
  • velle list marks adapters with the library they need.

Usage

Load the stylesheets in this order. The order matters: component styles override the base styles, and utilities override components.

<head>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/css/velle/reset.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/css/velle/variables.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/css/velle/base.css">

  <!-- component stylesheets, in alphabetical order -->
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/css/velle/button.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/css/velle/dialog.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/css/velle/icons.css">

  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/css/velle/utilities.css">

  <!-- behaviors you use; each one loads velle.js itself -->
  <script type="module" src="/assets/js/velle/dialog.js"></script>
</head>

Keep component stylesheets in alphabetical order, as css-zero did. A few rules have equal specificity and rely on it, for example .btn and .avatar on the same <button class="btn avatar">. The bundled dist/velle.css is already in this order.

Then write plain HTML:

<button type="button" class="btn btn--primary" commandfor="welcome" command="show-modal">Open</button>

<dialog id="welcome" class="dialog" data-dialog data-dialog-action="click->closeOnClickOutside">
  <div class="dialog__content">Hello!</div>
</dialog>

How it fits together

Tokens
CSS custom properties for colors, sizes, typography, shadows and animations, in variables.css.
Base
reset.css normalizes the browser defaults. base.css defines the semantic colors (--color-bg, --color-text, --color-primary…), with light and dark values chosen by light-dark(). Edit base.css to theme everything.
Components
BEM-style classes such as .btn, .btn--primary and .card__footer. Most options are CSS variables you can set inline, e.g. style="--dialog-size: 32rem".
Utilities
Small single-purpose classes for layout and spacing, such as .flex, .gap and .mbe-4, using logical properties.
JavaScript
Interactive components use data attributes and a tiny runtime with no dependencies. Native HTML does the rest: <dialog>, popover, invoker commands and <details>.

Browser support

velle-css targets current versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, and uses modern platform features directly: light-dark(), relative colors, the popover attribute, CSS anchor positioning, invoker commands (commandfor/command), @starting-style, :user-invalid, field-sizing, interpolate-size and view transitions. Animations degrade gracefully: accordions open instantly where ::details-content is missing. Features such as popover placement and opening dialogs with invoker commands only work in browsers that support them.

Differences from css-zero

  • No Rails, Hotwire or Stimulus. The Stimulus controllers were rewritten as vanilla JavaScript on a small runtime with the same lifecycle; see JavaScript.
  • Markup changes from data-controller="tabs" to data-tabs, from data-action="tabs#select" to data-tabs-action="select", and from data-x-name-value to data-x-name. Targets keep the data-x-target form.
  • back_navigation was removed: it depended on Turbo's history tracking.
  • turbo_confirm is now confirm and works with plain forms and links through data-confirm.
  • Icons and other images are inlined in the CSS, so stylesheets work from any path or CDN.
  • The Rails-only .field_with_errors and turbo-frame rules were removed; aria-invalid="true" marks server-side errors.
  • command, dropzone, dual_range, input_otp and resizable were rebuilt in plain JavaScript and no longer need a library. dropzone submits files with the form instead of Rails direct uploads.
  • combobox is now the browser's customizable <select> instead of tom-select, so it no longer offers free-text search or tagging.
  • chart, datepicker, inputmask and sortable are adapters: you install Chart.js, flatpickr, maska or SortableJS yourself.
  • sound was removed. The Lexxy rich text editor is planned for a later release.
